ja: 先ほどのご質問ですが、営業部長は先月、新しい価格は4月から適用されると私たちに言っていました。
en: Regarding the earlier question, the sales director told us last month that the new prices would take effect in April.
alternatives: About the earlier question, the sales director told us last month that the new prices would start in April.
As for the earlier question, the sales director told us last month that the new pricing would start in April.
point: 過去の発言を伝えるので will ではなく would にする

ja: 発表の前に、プロジェクターの電源を入れてもらえますか？
en: Could you turn on the projector before the presentation?
alternatives: Can you turn on the projector before the presentation?
Could you switch on the projector before the presentation?
point: 「電源を入れる」は turn on。依頼は Could you で丁寧に

ja: 皆さんは、来年この新しいシステムを導入することについてどう思いますか？
en: What do you think about introducing this new system next year?
alternatives: How do you feel about introducing this new system next year?
What are your thoughts on introducing this new system next year?
point: about の後ろは to introduce ではなく introducing

ja: では、最初のスライドから始めましょう。
en: Let's start with the first slide.
alternatives: Let's begin with the first slide.
Let's start from the first slide.
point: 提案は Let's＋動詞の原形。first の前に the を忘れずに

ja: 私たちが一番心配しているのは、納期に間に合わないことではなく、品質が落ちることです。
en: What we're most worried about isn't missing the deadline but a drop in quality.
alternatives: What concerns us most isn't missing the deadline, but the quality going down.
Our biggest concern isn't missing the deadline but a drop in quality.
point: What we're worried about の about を落とさない

ja: このプランはコストを下げるだけでなく、導入期間も半分に短縮できます。
en: Not only does this plan reduce costs, but it also cuts the rollout time in half.
alternatives: Not only does this plan lower costs, but it also cuts the implementation period in half.
Not only will this plan reduce costs, but it'll also halve the rollout time.
point: Not only の後は does this plan reduce と疑問文の語順

ja: このプロジェクトで、私たちは半年間ずっと顧客データを分析してきました。
en: We've been analyzing customer data for six months on this project.
alternatives: For this project, we've been analyzing customer data for six months.
We've been analyzing customer data on this project for the past six months.
point: 今も続く「ずっと〜してきた」は have been + -ing

ja: 恐れ入りますが、ご質問をもう少し詳しくご説明いただけないでしょうか。
en: I was wondering if you could explain your question in a little more detail.
alternatives: Would you mind explaining your question in a bit more detail?
Could you possibly explain your question in a little more detail?
point: I was wondering if で丁寧に頼む。過去形でも今の依頼

ja: 質疑応答に入る前に、今日のポイントをもう一度ざっと振り返ってもいいですか？
en: Before we open it up for questions, could I quickly go over today's key points one more time?
alternatives: Before we move on to questions, can I quickly go over the main points from today once more?
Before we take questions, could I quickly run through today's key points again?
point: 「振り返る」は go over / run through の句動詞で

ja: うちの部長が昨日データを確認してくれていたら、私は今、質疑応答で数字を訂正しなくて済んだんですが。
en: If our manager had checked the data yesterday, I wouldn't have to correct these figures now during the Q&A.
alternatives: If our manager had checked the data yesterday, I wouldn't need to correct these figures now in the Q&A.
If our manager had gone over the data yesterday, I wouldn't have to fix these numbers now during the Q&A.
point: 過去の条件は had checked、今の結果は wouldn't have to

ja: 次に、私から今年の売上をお見せします。
en: Next, I'm going to show you this year's sales.
alternatives: Next, I'll show you this year's sales.
Now I'm going to show you our sales for this year.
point: これからすることは I'm going to / I'll で表す

ja: もし予算が今の倍あったとしたら、皆さんはこの提案のどの部分を最初に広げますか？
en: If you had twice the current budget, which part of this proposal would you expand first?
alternatives: If your budget were twice what it is now, which part of this proposal would you expand first?
If you had double the current budget, which part of this proposal would you scale up first?
point: 今の事実と違う仮定は過去形、問いは would you

ja: 質疑応答で先方の女性担当者が、もう外した機能について聞いてきたので、きっと彼女は提案書を読み違えたんでしょう。
en: The client's rep must have misread our proposal, since during the Q&A she asked about a feature we'd already dropped.
alternatives: The woman from the client must have misunderstood our proposal, because during the Q&A she asked about a feature we'd already removed.
During the Q&A, the client's rep asked about a feature we had already dropped, so she must have misread our proposal.
point: 過去への強い推量は must have + 過去分詞

ja: 発表のあとで、うちの部長が質問に答えます。
en: Our manager will answer questions after the presentation.
alternatives: Our manager is going to answer questions after the presentation.
Our manager will take questions after the presentation.
point: これからのことなので will か be going to を使う

ja: 新しい料金プランに関する資料は、会議の後で皆さんにメールでお送りします。
en: I'll email everyone the materials on the new pricing plan after the meeting.
alternatives: I'll send you all the materials about the new pricing plan by email after the meeting.
After the meeting, I'll email you the materials on the new pricing plan.
point: 「〜に関する資料」は materials on/about 〜 と後ろから修飾

ja: 今回の発表は、技術的な細かい話からではなく、顧客アンケートの結果から始めればよかったと思っています。
en: I wish I'd opened the presentation with the customer survey results instead of diving into the technical details.
alternatives: I wish I had started the presentation with the customer survey results rather than the technical details.
I should have opened the presentation with the customer survey results instead of getting into the technical details.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を had + 過去分詞にする

ja: 田中さんが質問したとき、私はまだグラフを説明していました。
en: I was still explaining the graph when Tanaka-san asked a question.
alternatives: I was still going over the graph when Tanaka-san asked me a question.
When Tanaka-san asked a question, I was still explaining the graph.
point: 途中だった動作は was ＋ -ing、割り込んだ動作は過去形

ja: データを見直した結果、私たちのチームは当初の予測を下方修正することにしました。
en: Having reviewed the data, our team decided to revise our original forecast downward.
alternatives: After reviewing the data, our team decided to lower our original forecast.
Our team reviewed the data and decided to revise our initial forecast downward.
point: 先に終えたことは Having + 過去分詞で文頭に置ける

ja: 山田さんがご指摘のとおり、この問題は去年からずっと議論されてきました。
en: As Ms. Yamada pointed out, this issue has been discussed since last year.
alternatives: As Ms. Yamada mentioned, this issue has been under discussion since last year.
As Ms. Yamada pointed out, we've been discussing this issue since last year.
point: 「去年から議論されてきた」は has been discussed

ja: ご質問にお答えする前に、担当のエンジニアに技術的な詳細を説明させます。
en: Before I take your questions, I'll have the engineer in charge explain the technical details.
alternatives: Before I answer your questions, I'll have the engineer in charge walk you through the technical details.
Before taking your questions, I'll have our engineer in charge explain the technical details.
point: have 人 do は原形。to explain にしない

ja: もし君がスライドの数字の間違いを指摘してくれていなかったら、僕は役員会で間違った数字を発表していたよ。
en: If you hadn't pointed out the error in the slides, I'd have presented the wrong numbers to the board.
alternatives: If you hadn't caught the mistake in the slides, I would have shown the board the wrong figures.
I would have presented the wrong numbers to the board if you hadn't pointed out the error on the slides.
point: 過去の仮定は if 節が had 過去分詞、主節は would have

ja: これからお見せするデータは、私たちが先月実施した顧客調査に基づいています。
en: The data I'm about to show you is based on a customer survey that we conducted last month.
alternatives: The data I'm going to show you is based on a customer survey we carried out last month.
The data I'll be showing you comes from a customer survey that we ran last month.
point: 「私たちが実施した調査」は survey (that) we conducted と後ろに置く

ja: この資料には、グラフが全部で3つあります。
en: There are three charts in this handout.
alternatives: This handout has three charts.
There are three graphs in this handout.
point: 複数あるなら There are、場所は文の最後に置く

ja: 前回の発表以降、私たちは新たに200社の顧客を獲得しましたが、そのほとんどは先月契約したばかりです。
en: Since our last presentation, we've gained 200 new clients, but we signed most of them just last month.
alternatives: We've added 200 new clients since our last presentation, but most of them only signed last month.
Since the last presentation, we've won 200 new clients, though we signed most of them just last month.
point: since は現在完了、last month は過去形と使い分ける

ja: 今日皆さんにお伝えしたいのは、この変更がなぜ今必要なのかということです。
en: What I want to tell you today is why this change is necessary right now.
alternatives: What I'd like to share with you today is why we need this change now.
What I want to explain today is why this change is needed right now.
point: 文頭の What I want to tell you を主語にし、is の後は why 節

ja: この提案を役員会で承認してもらうには、私たちは他にどんなデータを用意すべきでしょうか。
en: What other data should we prepare to get this proposal approved by the board?
alternatives: What other data do we need to prepare to get the board to approve this proposal?
To get this proposal approved by the board, what other data should we prepare?
point: 「〜してもらうには」は目的の to get 〜 approved で表す
